correctness.rationale: For each arrival t, the event that the fixed set S has no children is precisely the restriction P_t outside earlier S; because the original P_t are independent, conditioning preserves independence and makes each surviving birth attach uniformly to an earlier surviving birth. This proves the whole-tree erasure law for all n and fixed S. The known depth pgf is independently derived from the parent recursion. Telescoping gives P(i leaf)=(i-1)/(n-1), proving each indexed covariance and their sum, with appropriate zero cases. A verified leaf-variance recurrence proves the correlation limit. The exact standalone verifier passes 17,014 distribution and moment assertions on every recursive tree through n=8. Enumeration is not substituted for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The established published comparisons provide marginal birth-label depth distributions, overall outdegree/leaf-count fluctuations, and different random-deletion laws. None of the inspected mathematical statements or accessible earlier claims implies the full fixed-terminal-label conditioned uniform-tree law, its joint generating functions for arbitrary sets, or the position-specific depth/leaf covariance profile. The comparison is not a proof of universal priority; an inaccessible earlier subtree-leaf article and broad enumeration literature are residual historical risks.
residual_risks: Full text of Mahmoud and Smythe (1991) and some historical survey/book treatments was not available, so historical priority remains qualified.
The all-set conditional erasure law follows from a short independent-parent argument and might be implicit in a general sampling-consistency theorem not found during bounded searches.
Search results and the inspected passages do not constitute independent priority certification.

value.rationale: Conditional removal of designated terminal birth labels is a motivated structural sampling-consistency question for recursive genealogies. The exact law describes an entire probability measure and a family of set-indexed joint depth/leaf-event generating functions, not an arbitrary special numerical case. Its strict stochastic depth reduction and universal negative birth-label depth/total-leaf covariance profile supply directly interpretable finite-scale dependence. This is not a generic marginal result or a relabeling of the earlier sum-of-depths covariance.
